text:
Five games without a win, four of them regulation losses, and a 4-3 defeat in Philadelphia on Tuesday where, as Matthew Fairburn of The Athletic pointed out, the Sabres had more giveaways (20) than shots on goal (19). Buffalo is 8-9-4 and the mood matches the record.

The chances say it's partly real. They had 46% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) during the winless run. Over the full season they sit at 49%, a roughly even team that has scored almost nine fewer goals than its chances earned. That finishing gap is the difference between this and a team hanging around the wild-card line. Our odds give them a 19% shot at the playoffs.

The goaltending has been a storyline all month. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen was pulled in the rout against Tampa Bay, Colten Ellis struggled in relief, and Alex Lyon only made his season debut on Nov. 12. There are bright spots: the Jack Quinn, Noah Ostlund and Zach Benson line takes 59% of the expected goals and 65% of the shot attempts, and Owen Power with Olen Zellweger has been the better pair. The question for Lindy Ruff is whether the finishing turns before the season does.
